text:
All shall be well, and all shall be well,
and all manner of thing shall be well.
meaning: Words given to the English mystic Julian of Norwich in a vision in 1373, and among the most quoted lines of comfort in English.
purpose: To hold on to hope in grief or fear.
note: From Julian of Norwich’s Revelations of Divine Love, chapter 27. In her own Middle English: "al shal be wel and al shal be wel and all manner of thyng shal be wele."
source: Julian of Norwich, Revelations of Divine Love, ch. 27 (CCEL edition)
name: All Shall Be Well
